commit.message:
fix(translator): guard against doubled tool-call args from openai-compat providers

- replace buffer when provider streams cumulative args (chunk restates full string)
- finish block idempotent: repeated finish_reason no longer re-emits buffered args
- sanitizeToolArgs halves exact-doubled JSON ({...}{...}) as last resort

Observed: opencode/mimo-v2.5-free delivered tool args doubled in 975 calls
across 7 sessions; client rejected all as "Invalid tool parameters".
Gateway saw HTTP 200 so no failover ever triggered.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

fix(translator): drop harness XML blocks echoed by the model into visible output

Some models (gemini family: 188 of 204 observed echo turns) repeat the
client harness wrapper blocks (<instructions>, <system-reminder>,
<task-notification>, <command-message>, <command-name>) verbatim in their
visible text. Streaming-safe filter drops those blocks from text deltas:
tags split across chunks are held via state.echoCarry; non-tag "<..."
prefixes flush at finish; unclosed echo blocks are discarded.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

fix(combo): retry aborted streams before first output

Preflight SSE bodies before committing a combo member so 200-then-abort and empty streams cascade. Preserve exact bytes after first output; cancel upstream readers; add focused regression tests.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

fix(discipline): demote models that emit malformed tool JSON

Three malformed tool-JSON strikes on the same serving model trip the
existing 30-second per-model lock through the status-400
markAccountUnavailable path. The strike entry expires after ten minutes
of inactivity, and the malformed counter resets once a lock fires so a
recovered model is not immediately re-locked.

Non-corruption strikes (echo drops, think-aloud) are tracked for
observability but excluded from the lock threshold, so only genuine
tool-JSON corruption can demote a model.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

feat(discipline): nudge a model after malformed output

A model that emits doubled tool-call JSON or echoes the harness XML
wrapper into visible output now gets one corrective system line on its
next request, injected through the existing systemInject seam beside
caveman and ponytail.

Echoed harness XML now records a strike at the drop site. It never
counts toward the 30-second lock threshold — only doubled-json does —
but it arms the nudge, so an echoing model is corrected rather than
silently filtered forever.

The nudge keys on `${provider}/${model}`, matching how stream.js builds
state.servingModel; a mismatch there would leave strikes and nudges in
separate buckets and the nudge would never fire.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

test(discipline): cover the account-lock callback seam

The strike store was unit-tested but the wiring between it and
markAccountUnavailable was not: argument order, the 400 status used for
the lock, the reason string, and the guarantee that a rejected lock is
swallowed rather than escaping into the response stream.

Extracts the callback into buildDisciplineLock so that seam is testable
without standing up a request, and covers it with four cases including a
rejecting lock and a throwing error handler.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

feat(usage): persist combo, chain depth and session attribution

Adds comboName, chainDepth and sessionId to usageHistory, indexed on the
two that get filtered on. migrate.js adds missing columns automatically
from TABLES, so this needs no hand-written migration; SCHEMA_VERSION goes
to 2 so the pre-change backup runs first.

saveRequestUsage persists the three fields and saveUsageStats accepts
them, defaulting to NULL/0. They are nullable by design: a direct
(non-combo) request has no combo and no cascade depth, and sessionId is
only set when the client sends one.

Upstream callers do not supply these values yet — combo.js knows
comboName and the cascade index, but neither is threaded down to the
usage writer. That threading is the remaining half of A3.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

feat(usage): populate sessionId on usage rows

chatCore already resolves the client session for log tagging via
sessionManager.resolveSessionId. Passing it through sharedCtx puts it in
reach of every usage writer at once, since all four response paths
(forced-SSE-to-JSON, non-streaming, streaming, stream-complete) spread
that same object — no callback contract had to change.

Each of the four saveUsageStats call sites now forwards sessionId, so
usageHistory.sessionId is populated instead of always NULL.

comboName and chainDepth remain NULL/0: comboName stops at
combo.js handleSingleModel(body, modelStr), whose contract would have to
widen to carry the combo and its cascade index. That is the remaining
piece of A3.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

feat(usage): populate comboName and chainDepth on usage rows

handleComboChat now passes the cascade position as a third argument to
its handleSingleModel callback, and chat.js threads that plus the combo
name (which it already had as modelStr) down through
handleSingleModelChat into handleChatCore. From there both ride
sharedCtx to all four usage writers, the same path sessionId takes.

The third argument is safe: handleFusionChat's callback also takes a
third parameter, isPanel, but that is a different closure and is not the
one handleComboChat invokes.

A direct single-model request leaves comboName null and chainDepth 0, so
non-combo traffic is unchanged. Completes A3: usageHistory now records
which combo served a request, how deep in its fallback cascade the
request landed, and the client session it belongs to.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

fix(api): require a dashboard session to mutate combos

POST /api/combos and PUT/DELETE /api/combos/[id] rewrite and delete routing
configuration, and this app has no middleware.js — nothing guarded them. On a
publicly reachable host that means anyone who can hit the origin could add,
reorder or delete combo members.

Adds the same check /api/auth/oidc/test already uses: requireLogin=false still
short-circuits for local-only installs, otherwise a valid auth_token dashboard
session is required. GET is deliberately left open so the dashboard can list
combos without a session; reads expose no capability a logged-out caller can
act on.

This is what A2 actually needed. The REST surface for membership and order
already existed and works — PUT passes the models array straight to
updateCombo and resets rotation state on change. The missing half of
"authenticated REST for combo membership/order" was the authentication.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

feat(combo): skip models still inside their cooldown window

The cascade already learned when a model wanted to be left alone — it read
retryAfter from the error body and took cooldownMs from checkFallbackError —
but only used that for the final error response and for an inline sleep of at
most 5 seconds. Nothing survived the request, so the next one walked straight
back into a model that had just said it was unavailable.

modelCooldown.js remembers the window per model. The cascade skips a model that
is still cooling down and logs the remaining time; if every model is cooling
down the loop falls through to the existing exhausted path unchanged, so no
request loses its fallback.

Bounded by model cardinality, expired entries dropped on read, module-level Map
with synchronous access so no locking is involved.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

feat(combo): skip quota-exhausted models and track model health

Two behaviours the cascade was missing.

Quota exhaustion is not a cooldown. A 402, or a 429 that names quota, balance
or a daily/monthly limit, means the model is gone for hours — so it is
remembered separately with an hour-long window and skipped at the head of the
cascade instead of being rediscovered one request at a time. Plain per-minute
rate limiting is explicitly NOT treated as exhaustion; that stays a normal
cooldown, so a busy model is not benched for an hour.

Health tracking counts consecutive failures per model and clears the run on any
success, so a model that recovers returns on its own with no operator action.
demoteUnhealthy reorders without dropping: a combo whose models are all sick
still tries all of them.

Both stores are module-level Maps with synchronous access, bounded by model
cardinality, expired entries dropped on read. Every skip path falls through to
the existing exhausted-combo response, so no request loses its fallback.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

fix(combo): actually apply health demotion, and test the wiring

demoteUnhealthy was exported and unit-tested but never called from the
cascade. Health was recorded on every failure and success and then thrown
away — the demotion half of the feature did not exist in production while
every unit test passed.

It now runs after rotation and capability auto-switch, so a model with a run
of consecutive failures is tried last. Ordering only; nothing is dropped, and
a combo whose models are all sick still tries all of them.

Adds tests/unit/combo-skip.test.js, which asserts what the cascade DOES rather
than what the stores hold: a cooling-down model is not called, a quota
exhausted model is not called, a demoted model is not tried first, and when
every model is skipped the cascade falls through to the exhausted path instead
of reporting success. Deleting any of the three wirings fails one of these.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

feat(translator): drop a model regurgitating the user's own message

Session 7697af0e ended with an abusive user line coming back verbatim as
assistant output. The existing echo filter could not catch it: that one keys on
harness XML tags, and this is the user's own prose with nothing to match on.

stream.js already had the request body in scope, so the last user turn travels
with the stream state — no caller signature changed. The translator judges the
accumulated visible text, not each chunk, because regurgitation only becomes
recognisable once enough of it has arrived.

Deliberately conservative: only a verbatim prefix of at least 120 characters
counts, so a model quoting a line back at the user is never touched. Getting
this wrong deletes real answers, which is worse than the disease. A drop also
records an echo strike, so the A5 nudge corrects the model on its next request
instead of silently filtering it forever.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

fix(translator): filter echoed output on non-streaming replies too

The echo filters only ever ran on the streaming path. nonStreamingHandler has
its own translation route (translateNonStreamingResponse), so the same model
output was clean when streamed and dirty when not — echoed harness XML and
verbatim regurgitation of the user's message both passed straight through on
any non-streamed reply. That gap predates the user-echo work: the original
harness-XML filter shipped with it.

echoScrub.js does whole-text scrubbing, which is all a non-streaming body needs
— no carry buffer or state machine, since the text arrives at once. It handles
the three response shapes the router emits: OpenAI choices, Claude content
blocks, and Gemini candidate parts.

A scrub records an echo strike so the discipline nudge corrects the model,
matching the streaming path. scrubResponseBody returns false for a clean body
so no false strike is recorded, and the call is wrapped so scrubbing can never
break a response.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

fix(translator): scrub echoed output on the forced-SSE-to-JSON path

Third response path with the same blind spot. When a provider insists on
streaming but the client wants JSON, sseToJsonHandler assembles the chunks into
a body via parseSSEToOpenAIResponse — so the streaming filter never sees it and
the non-streaming scrub is not on this route either. Echoed harness XML and
verbatim regurgitation both passed through.

All three paths are now covered: streaming filters incrementally in
openai-to-claude.js, and both JSON-producing paths scrub the assembled body.

The underlying shape is worth naming: the filter has three call sites that must
be kept in sync, which is why the gap survived two rounds of fixing. The right
structure is one scrub inside the translator layer that every path routes
through. Left as a follow-up rather than attempted here, because it touches
every response route at once.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

fix(translator): echo-filter the second Claude output path

kiro-to-claude is the other translator that emits Claude content_block_delta
text, and it had no echo guards at all — a model could parrot harness XML or
return the user's own message verbatim and it would reach the client untouched.

Rather than copy the filters, openai-to-claude now exports them and kiro-to-claude
imports them. Duplicating this logic is precisely how it came to be missing from
two of three response paths; one implementation cannot drift from itself.

Filtering happens before the content block bookkeeping so that a fully dropped
chunk does not open an empty text block.

Nine other translators still have no echo filtering. They translate to OpenAI,
Gemini and Antigravity shapes rather than Claude, so they are not on the
claude-9r path — recorded in the vault rather than changed blind.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

fix(combo): score throw-class failures so dead-stream models get demoted

The cascade catch branch recorded neither success nor failure, so a model whose
failure mode is "HTTP 200 then the stream ends before the first event"
(preflight throws with comboFallbackStatus 502) stayed permanently healthy and
kept its lead position. Observed in production: oc/nemotron-3-ultra-free sits at
index 0 of Fenrir, fails every request, and is never demoted.

Status-path failures already score at the returned-Response branch; this adds
the same call to the catch branch so throw-class failures reach the demotion
threshold like any other.

Tests: 5 files / 29 passed (was 3 / 17). The two assertions that pinned the hole
as correct behaviour are flipped, plus a new case proving a throw-only model
loses first place after the threshold.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
fix(combo): skip models below request context

fix(stream): close SSE cleanly on all termination paths

Two controller.error() sites at the response boundary leaked [CommandCode
error: "Upstream stream ended before terminal chunk"] into visible text
when upstream crashed, stalled, or timed out. The harness wraps any
ReadableStream error as a transport error; the model then prints the
wrapped error as if it were a tool failure.

- streamHandler.js: createDisconnectAStream always calls controller.close()
  instead of branching on isNetworkClose/wasConnected to decide between
  close() and error(). Every termination — network reset, timeout, abort,
  upstream crash — now closes the SSE stream cleanly.
- combo.js: preflightSseResponse (its own ReadableStream, outside the
  createDisconnectAStream path) now calls controller.close() instead of
  controller.error() on upstream read failure.

A rule (V4) cannot prevent this — the bytes arrive in a tool_result
regardless. The fix belongs at the transport layer. inyund fork branch.
Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

@
feat(tuner): port tuner into 9router, add /api/tuner routes

Move tune.mjs, bench.json, discover.mjs into tuner/ directory,
baked into the image. No more shared volume for tuner logic.

GET /api/tuner: public, read-only state. No auth token needed.
POST /api/tuner/run|pin|policy: dashboard JWT-gated.
Dockerfile copies tuner/ into image.
dashboardGuard adds /api/tuner to PUBLIC_API_PATHS.

Co-Authored-By: Claude <noreply@anthropic.com>
@

fix(providers): count all auth types in dualAuthTypes when provider has no declared authModes

Providers without authModes (e.g. ollama) defaulted to oauth-only in
dualAuthTypes, so apikey connections were invisible on the list page
card (total=0) while showing correctly on the detail page.

Return all three auth types when no modes are declared, matching the
intent documented on freeTierEntries.

Co-Authored-By: Claude <noreply@anthropic.com>

fix(chat): remove stale cacheClaudeHeaders import removed upstream

Upstream v0.5.50 deleted open-sse/utils/claudeHeaderCache.js in 13ed1456,
but the inyund patch added it back during rebase. Unused import — drop it.

feat(tuner): bottom-prefix sort — cmc/ocg always last in every combo

Split+concat pushes cmc/ and ocg/ providers to end after interleave.
Bench-configurable via _bottomPrefixes.prefixes list.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
chore: remove dead open-sse/services/compact.js

test: update golden-url-header snapshot

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

refactor(combo): decide every skip in one place and log it at warn

Three filters — context fit, quota exhaustion, model cooldown — each decided
independently in the cascade loop and announced at info. A combo could pass over
every entry that had quota and answer from its last one, with nothing in the log
at normal verbosity to say the earlier entries were never attempted.

Collapse them into shouldSkipModel(), which returns the reason so the caller can
report it, and raise skipped entries to warn. No routing behaviour changes.

Adds the regression cases from the investigation; six describe behaviour the
cascade does not yet have and are registered in known-fails until the follow-up
lands.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

fix(combo): skip a model only when no account can serve it

A quota error from whichever account happened to be picked banned the model
process-wide for an hour. Every other account of that provider was passed over
for the rest of that hour — including accounts with untouched quota, accounts
whose window had since reset, and accounts re-enabled or added in the meantime.
A combo with several Antigravity entries would route past all of them to a
provider far down the list, and stay there.

The account layer already tracks which accounts are locked and until when. The
cascade now asks it, via a canServe probe supplied by the caller, and its own
per-model quota/cooldown maps become the standalone fallback for when no account
layer is present.

Three things fed the ban and are fixed with it:

- The ban ran for a fixed hour regardless of what the provider said. It now
  expires at the provider's reported reset time when one is given.
- The router's "all accounts locked" reply quotes the provider's text, and was
  read back as fresh evidence — letting one 429 renew its own ban indefinitely.
  That reply is now marked as our synthesis and carries the real retryAfter.
- The context-window filter counted the request's output budget against the
  model's input window, silently removing 200k-window models from long
  conversations. Only the input is weighed now.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

fix(combo): report the status of the error the response quotes

When every entry failed, the status came from the first failure and the message
from the last, so a client could receive one provider's code explaining a
different provider's error — a 410 from an entry that was never mentioned,
carrying a 400 about an invalid API key. Clients act on the status: a code that
says "don't retry" ends a request that a retry would have served.

Status and message now move together, on the returned-Response path and the
thrown-exception path alike.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

fix(combo): treat an absent account-layer opinion as silence, not capacity

Review of the previous commit found the account probe was allowed to speak for
providers it knows nothing about. Four fixes, all in that seam:

The probe returned "serveable" unconditionally for no-auth free providers
(opencode, mimo-free, mmf, devin-cli). No account lock is ever written for those
— there is no account — so the cascade skipped its own quota memory for them and
re-tried an exhausted daily quota at the head of the cascade on every request,
forever. The probe now answers null for anything it has no per-account state for,
including providers with nothing configured, and null means "decide for
yourself" rather than "go ahead".

An entry skipped by the probe never reached handleSingleModel, so a combo whose
providers were all locked returned a bare 503 with no detail and no Retry-After
— worse than the per-entry errors it replaced. Skips now carry the lock expiry
the probe already had in hand.

A retryAfter that parsed to the past — as a bare `retryAfter: 30` does, being
read as an epoch offset — produced a zero-length quota ban, which is no ban at
all. Only a reset time in the future now replaces the default window.

The probe cost a model resolution plus a connections query per entry per
request, uncached, which under the pure-JS SQLite fallback is not free. It is
now memoized for the life of one request and no longer.

Also: a permanent-looking status from a trailing entry no longer buries a
retryable one from an earlier entry, so a combo whose first model was merely
rate-limited stops reporting itself as a permanent client error.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

fix(combo): let a demoted model earn its way back without a success

Demotion moves a failing model behind the healthy ones, and the run only cleared
on a success. But a demoted model is never tried while a healthy one ahead of it
keeps answering, and a model that is never tried can never succeed — so three
failures exiled it permanently.

Observed in production: four of six entries in a combo were demoted, the first
survivor was skipped for exceeding its context window, and every request landed
on the one remaining healthy entry. The 1M-window Antigravity model that should
have absorbed those requests had not been tried in hours — it produced no log
line at all, not even a skip.

Failure runs now age out. After a quiet spell the model returns to its natural
position and gets one ordinary attempt; if it is still broken a fresh run of
failures demotes it again, costing one round trip per window. A failure after
the window restarts the run rather than resuming it, so a stale failure and a
fresh one cannot add up to a demotion.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

fix(antigravity): honour the quota reset the provider states

An Antigravity 429 carries the exact moment the quota returns — an absolute
quotaResetTimeStamp plus two Go-style durations. None of it was read, so a
week-long exhaustion was locked with a generic backoff and re-tried every five
minutes: observed in production as six accounts each burning 3-15s per request
to be told "Resets in 162h57m59s" again.

The executor now parses all three forms, and a hard quota is allowed to hold its
account past the 30-minute cap that exists for rolling rate limits.

A 403 also stops being treated as congestion. It is a permission decision that
two minutes of waiting cannot change — the account was refused, not throttled —
so it gets a long cooldown, and the connection is marked "expired" rather than
"unavailable" so the dashboard shows an account needing re-authorization instead
of one that is merely busy.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

fix(tuner): derive bands from declared model identity, not id substrings

A model id is a wire name, not a description: `ag/gemini-3.1-pro-low` carries
a route, a capability class and an effort in one opaque string. matchBench
recovered the middle one by substring-scanning the whole id, and that guess
failed in both directions on the same model - `gemini-3.1-pro-low` matched
`gemini-3.1-pro` and inherited an opus band it never earned, while
`gemini-pro-agent`, the HIGH variant, matched nothing and was invisible to
every combo. That is how a fable-band combo came to serve the low variant for
two full sessions while the high one sat unused.

Registry model entries now declare `family`, `effort` and `mode`. Bands attach
to families in bench.models; effort shifts the band by a declared offset from
bench._effortBandOffset; mode never moves a band. Matching is exact -
substring inference is deleted, so `low` can no longer reach its family's tier
by any path. /v1/models carries the declared identity because the tuner is a
separate process that reads candidates from it, and bench._modelIdentity
covers candidates with no registry entry.

An unresolved candidate stays fail-closed and is now loud: every run names it,
says whether the family is undeclared or merely unbanded, records it in the
tuner state, and posts to the Discord webhook when the list changes.

Backfills the 83 entries across 24 registries that only banded via substring.
Five bands move, ag/gemini-pro-agent is banded for the first time, and 14 ids
lose a band they should not have had - TTS and image models being ranked as
chat models, plus gpt-5.3-codex-spark, its review variant and gpt-5.5-pro,
which are distinct models rather than variants and are left undeclared so they
surface in the report and get their own bench entries by hand.

Adds CONTEXT.md as the glossary and docs/adr/0001 for the decision; unignores
docs/adr/ so ADRs can be committed.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_01ENfADjYv7PrwrtD2abZZv2

fix(tuner): band gpt-5.3-codex-spark and gpt-5.5-pro on their own terms

Both were borrowing a neighbour's band through substring matching, and the
previous commit left them undeclared so they would surface in the unbanded
report. Closing that instead: each gets a family of its own name and its own
bench.json entry, which is what "it is a different model, not a variant"
actually implies.

Neither has a published benchmark, so both stay at the tier they already
effectively had rather than being promoted on price alone. gpt-5.3-codex-spark
prices at 3.00/12.00, between gpt-5.6-luna (haiku) and gpt-5.6-terra (opus),
so sonnet is where it already sat. gpt-5.5-pro prices at 30.00/180.00 - six
times gpt-5.6-sol - which argues for more, but price is a proxy and this file
bands from benchmarks; the note records the evidence so it can be promoted
deliberately later.

The rule this makes explicit, now recorded in the ADR: when the evidence is
thin, band LOW. Understating a model costs it work it could have done;
overstating it puts it in a combo it has not earned, which is the failure the
ADR exists to prevent.

Every remaining band loss is now a TTS, image or STT model that was being
ranked as a chat model - no judgement calls left open.

Also closes three loose ends around the change itself: a CHANGELOG entry under
the `# Unreleased` heading the repo already uses; a comment on the .gitignore
exception, verified to expose docs/adr/ and nothing else; and a CLAUDE.md note
on the Windows exec-bit trap, which reports three files as permanently
modified with zero content change and blocks `git stash pop`.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_01ENfADjYv7PrwrtD2abZZv2

fix(tuner): declare identity for the free-tier ids that had none

Deleting substring inference dropped 17 candidates out of their combos at
once, because they reach the tuner from the DB as custom models registered
against a provider node - not from /v1/models - so there is no registry entry
to carry a family and nothing left to match on. Observed in production
immediately after deploy: Odin lost its free fable head
(tokenrouter/moonshotai/kimi-k3-free), Sleipnir lost its free head
(oc/deepseek-v4-flash-free), and Valkyrie lost both laguna-s-2.1 entries.

Every one is a FREE-TIER id. A free tier is not an effort - it costs less, it
does not think less - so each declares its family with mode:free and keeps
that family's band unshifted. Verified against the live unbanded report: all
17 return to exactly the band they held before, no model moves anywhere else,
and the 62 candidates that were already unbanded stay unbanded.

bench._modelIdentity is the mechanism this change already added for exactly
this case; it shipped empty, which is the whole defect. The gap was in how I
checked, not in the rule: the pre-flight diff was computed over the registry,
so candidates that only exist in the DB were never in the sample.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_01ENfADjYv7PrwrtD2abZZv2

docs: add handoff for the remaining frame-integrity work

Records what the EDR-killed session left behind: the banding work is shipped
(87b88536..e9ff4daa) and deployed, so the only thing outstanding is frame
integrity. Also captures the conflict that has to be settled before ADR 0002 —
the repo already strips harness markers in echoScrub.js and the streaming
filter, which the settled "detect, never strip" design does not allow for.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_01AZRz2wVo5zgHSFByZzFNb5

feat(router): enforce frame integrity through the existing health signal

A model that emits the client harness's own control markers — the XML wrapper
blocks (<system-reminder>, <instructions>, …) or a control line such as
"[Request interrupted by user]" — is writing in a voice that is not its own.
The router owns the framing of a conversation and the client owns its content,
so this is a protocol violation, decidable by inspection and without judging
whether the answer was any good.

The router already reacted to part of this and inconsistently. Streaming and the
two assembled-body paths dropped harness tags; the Codex/Responses branch checked
nothing; and the tag list was declared twice in two files with no link between
them, so a marker added to one copy silently did not apply on the other path.
None of it reached the tuner: a model could forge the frame on every request and

fix(translator): keep a turn that produced nothing, so the model keeps its voice

A Gemini-served model would stop replying and start completing the user's
sentence — mid-word, in the user's voice, with a stray leading space or
period where it resumed. It read as corruption; it was the request.

Two rules combined to cause it. An assistant turn whose parts came out empty
was never pushed, and normalizeGeminiContents then merged whatever ended up
adjacent. Drop a model turn between two user turns and those user turns fuse.
In an agentic session, where every tool result arrives as a `user` turn, the
model's voice eroded a little each round until Gemini was handed a transcript
in which it had never spoken — an unfinished monologue, which it continued.
A six-round tool exchange lost half its model turns.

The echo scrubbers made it worse over time rather than better: each scrub
emptied an assistant turn, and the emptied turn was then dropped from the
next request, deepening the condition that produced the echo.

An empty turn now keeps its slot on every affected path — openai-to-gemini,
the Antigravity envelope, the tool_calls branch whose entries are skipped
when they are not `type: "function"`, and openai-to-claude, which dropped the
turn a hop earlier so the Gemini-side fix alone would not have held.

Two details the placeholder depends on, both found in review:
- It is non-whitespace. `hasValidContent` requires `block.text?.trim()`, so a
  blank placeholder is filtered straight back out and the turns fuse anyway —
  the fix would look present and do nothing.
- It is substituted at flush, never appended, so it cannot land beside real
  content: Anthropic rejects a text block with no non-whitespace text.
- It is never left trailing. A final assistant turn is a prefill the model
  continues from, which is this same defect entered from the other end.

findSpeakerBoundaryViolation asserts the invariant. It is diagnostic — it
logs and the request still goes out — so that a future edit reintroducing the
erasure is visible. The original went undiagnosed across several attempts
because nothing anywhere said the history had been rewritten.

1801 pass / 85 fail, verify-no-regression reports all known.

Failing over is the right response where deleting is not. A retry costs one
upstream call; a wrong deletion costs the answer. That asymmetry is why these
thresholds can be tighter than the echo filter's 120-char prefix rule, which
was tuned to miss both incidents — each was ~10 tokens and matched the tail.

response: a chunk budget, a 300ms wall clock that only runs when the stream
genuinely pauses, and stopping as soon as there is enough prose to judge. Two
existing invariants survive, and their tests pin them: an error met while
reading ahead is replayed rather than cascaded, so "no cascade once the first
chunk arrived" still holds, and a read left in flight when the budget expires
is carried into the replay rather than abandoned — a reader permits one read at
a time. An earlier draft of this got both wrong: it hung 5s on a quiet stream
and turned a late abort into a cascade.

refactor(router): replace the orchestration nudge with a language lock

The nudge stated a live novel-context count whenever a session passed a
delegation cap of 6. Two independent measurements retire it.

It was below its own break-even. A delegation costs a median 313,582 units
against 34,514 for a main-thread turn, so it is worth roughly nine inline turns.
Firing at six pushed every session it touched into a losing trade.

And it did not work. ADR 0003 conceded it "nudges and cannot compel"; session
dce6e9bd then made 23 further inline calls with the nudge firing at `firm` on all
five logged turns. An ineffective instruction attached to every request is not
free — it is a standing tax on the system prompt, and it teaches the model to
discount what the system prompt says.

In its place, rtk/languageLock.js pins every part of a response to one language
(NINER_RESPONSE_LANGUAGE, default English). Models in the cheaper bands reason in
Chinese and sometimes carry it into visible output: 135 Han occurrences across
223 transcripts, nearly all inside `thinking` blocks — which matters because this
operator runs the client in verbose mode and therefore reads the thinking.

Filtering the output was rejected. Stripping CJK would corrupt any legitimate
quotation of file content, and it treats the symptom at the last possible moment.
An instruction reaches the model before it generates, costs ~40 tokens, and is
the one class of directive models follow reliably.

ADR 0003 is marked superseded rather than deleted, since commit messages
reference it.

Two headroom assertions move from an exact `messages` array to
`expect.arrayContaining`. The language lock prepends a system message to every
outbound body; what those tests are about is that the compressed message reached
the executor and the original did not, and the assertion that pins that is
unchanged.

tuner: band the qwen3.8 line, and stop reporting an oversized request as an outage

Two unrelated failures that both ended in the same place: a combo with
nothing left to try.

qwen3.8-max was invisible to the tuner. band() resolves bench.models[family],
and no qwen3.8-max family existed, so bandOf() returned null and tune.mjs's
pool filter dropped it from every combo -- which is why adding it in the
dashboard never survived: tune.mjs recomputes the whole membership list and
PUTs it back, deleting anything not in its computed pool.

The registry stopgap that borrowed family "qwen3.7-max" could not have fixed
this on its own. The dashboard registers these as custom models against a
provider node, so they reach the tuner from the DB and never pass through
providers/registry at all. _modelIdentity is the path that carries identity
for DB-sourced ids, and it is checked first, so it also lands without a
redeploy. Both are declared now; either route resolves.

Three smaller holes in the same file would have sunk it anyway: prefix "tr"
was absent from costClass (so cost() returned the default 3, sorting it below
even subscription providers), from providerByPrefix, and from quotaScope.

Separately: a request larger than every context window in a combo was
answered 503. shouldSkipModel's window branch records lastStatus = 503 at the
skip site, the tail passes it through, and isRetryableStatus(503) is true --
so the client retries a condition that cannot change until the conversation
is compacted, forever. A window-size exhaustion is now 413
context_length_exceeded, naming the widest window available, and only when
NO entry was skipped for any other reason and none was actually attempted.

fix(usage): stop estimating base64 images as prose

estimateInputTokens stringified the whole body and divided by 4. An inlined
image arrives base64 — a data: URI in OpenAI content parts, a bare
source.data string in Anthropic ones — and base64 runs ~4/3 of the raw
bytes, so a 3MB phone photo scored over a million tokens where the provider
bills it around a thousand.

That estimate feeds the per-model context check in services/combo.js, so one
photo made every model in a combo look too small and the request was refused
with context_length_exceeded before it was ever sent. Observed on Yggdrasil:
~1083798 tokens against a 1048576 window, while the session's own meter read
~20K. Compaction could not help — compacting 226 history items moved the
total by 1516 tokens, because the bulk was never history.

Images are now excluded from the character count and charged a flat 1600
each, the ceiling of the published per-image ranges. estimateUsage shares the
estimator, so recorded usage and cost stop being inflated by attachments too.
